title: Retrieval, RAG, Agents, and Capstone Defense

weeks.focus: Define retrieval and answer outcomes, build an evaluation dataset, model exact and approximate search, and freeze F01-F08 predictions
Build hybrid retrieval, versioned evidence, grounded-answer evaluation, structured tools, authorization, approval, and durable state
Break and repair freshness, relevance, grounding, provider, replay, budget, and authorization claims
Integrate the final RFC, operating and migration evidence, defend Gate 6, assess, remediate, and publish a practice plan

readiness_note: Ready after portable lab tests, six isolated evaluator records, deterministic calibration checking, semantic and resource review, and focused and full-course validation passed on 2026-08-03.

outcomes.statement: Model exact and approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval and tune HNSW from measured recall, visited work, latency, memory, and index cost.
Build and compare chunked lexical, vector, filtered, hybrid, and reranked retrieval paths using one evaluation set.
Select retrieval, grounding, refusal, latency, and cost measures that connect to a declared user outcome and release gate.
Preserve evidence authorization, exact version, freshness, revocation, claim support, citations, and justified abstention.
Enforce versioned tool schemas, scoped credentials, deterministic authorization, bound human approval, and secret-free audit outside model output.
Resume, replay, deduplicate, cancel, compensate, and budget an agent workflow without repeating irreversible side effects.
Diagnose F01-F08 from immutable equivalent trials and connect each repair to user, security, operating, and cost consequences.
Defend the complete capstone across product, technical, security, operating, cost, ownership, migration, reversal, and organizational challenges.

challenge_questions.prompt: Which claim in your artifact most directly supports this outcome, and what evidence could falsify it: Model exact and approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval and tune HNSW from measured recall, visited work, latency, memory, and index cost.

What unstated assumption could invalidate your treatment of this outcome, and how would you test it: Build and compare chunked lexical, vector, filtered, hybrid, and reranked retrieval paths using one evaluation set.

Defend the causal chain behind your evidence for this outcome, including the first likely failure: Select retrieval, grounding, refusal, latency, and cost measures that connect to a declared user outcome and release gate.

Which reasonable alternative would challenge your treatment of this outcome, and under what evidence would it win: Preserve evidence authorization, exact version, freshness, revocation, claim support, citations, and justified abstention.

What operational, security, cost, or ownership consequence is least supported in your treatment of this outcome: Enforce versioned tool schemas, scoped credentials, deterministic authorization, bound human approval, and secret-free audit outside model output.

Where does your evidence stop transferring to production for this outcome, and how is that boundary disclosed: Resume, replay, deduplicate, cancel, compensate, and budget an agent workflow without repeating irreversible side effects.

What dissent should a skeptical reviewer raise about your treatment of this outcome, and what follow-up evidence would resolve it: Diagnose F01-F08 from immutable equivalent trials and connect each repair to user, security, operating, and cost consequences.

What changed belief or reversal condition follows from your work on this outcome, and where is it recorded: Defend the complete capstone across product, technical, security, operating, cost, ownership, migration, reversal, and organizational challenges.
